procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Says urology scoped him right after Thanksgiving and 'it was clean.' We never got a note - front desk to request it. Next scope in late summer.
No hematuria since. Breathing at baseline, no swelling, weight steady. Hearing aids working.
Exam: lungs clear, RRR, no edema.
A/P: HTN, HFpEF stable - continue. Bladder ca surveillance per urology, 11/2023 cystoscopy negative by pt report. BMP.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to urology for the November cystoscopy note per PCP. No reply as of today.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request for metoprolol tartrate 50 mg and HCTZ 25 mg, 90 days. Seen in January, labs fine. Approved, 3 refills each.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Independent, no falls, driving. PHQ-2 0. Hearing aids daily.
Bladder cancer: next surveillance scope this summer with urology.
HTN/HFpEF: no complaints. BP at goal. Lungs clear, no edema.
Colonoscopy due 2027. Vaccines current for the season.
Labs today.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Daughter made the appointment. Dry cough for about 3 months that won't go away, and his pants are loose - down from 163 lb in May to 147 today. Appetite off. No fever, no night sweats, no blood in sputum. Breathing no worse than usual, no leg swelling.
Exam: thinner in the face. Breath sounds decreased over the right upper chest; otherwise clear. No supraclavicular or cervical nodes. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P: Persistent cough with 7+ kg weight loss in a 40 pack-year former smoker with prior TB - concerning for malignancy. CXR today in our imaging suite. Cancelled the old screening CT order; will go straight to diagnostic CT depending on film. Daughter aware.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Comparison none available on plain film. Right upper lobe mass. Remaining lungs clear. No effusion. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contour normal.
reports.conclusion: Right upper lobe mass. CT chest recommended.

orders.reason: right upper lobe mass on CXR

documents.title: CXR result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt and daughter with CXR: mass in the right upper lung. Explained it needs a CT and likely a biopsy, that we can't call it cancer yet but have to treat it that seriously. CT chest with contrast ordered, scheduling for next week. They had good questions; daughter will come to everything.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Right upper lobe: 4.0 cm spiculated mass. No additional pulmonary nodules. No hilar or mediastinal lymph node enlargement. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Visualized adrenal glands, liver and bones without lesions.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm spiculated right upper lobe mass, highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy. No evidence of metastatic disease.

documents.title: CT result and referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed CT: 4 cm spiculated RUL mass, no spread seen on this scan. Spoke with pt and daughter. Urgent pulmonology referral sent; I called their office and they'll see him within 2 weeks. He asked straight out if it's cancer - told him most likely, and that no spread on CT is the best news we could have today.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Date of visit 08/06/2024. Received 08/08/2024.

Referral: RUL mass.
HPI: 69-year-old man, hypertension, heart failure, and low-grade bladder urothelial carcinoma resected in 2023, with three months of persistent cough and unexplained weight loss. No fever, sweats or hemoptysis. Pulmonary TB treated about 20 years ago.
Meds: lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81 (HCTZ per patient). NKDA.
Social: 40 pack-years, quit 2012.
Exam: cachectic appearance. Diminished breath sounds over the right upper lobe. No palpable lymphadenopathy.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7,500, plt 250,000, Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.0, Ca 10.2, alk phos 120, CEA 11.4 (elevated).
Imaging: CXR with RUL mass; CT 4 cm spiculated RUL mass without evidence of metastasis.
Impression: RUL mass, likely primary lung cancer.
Plan: PET-CT for staging, then CT-guided core biopsy. Will discuss at our thoracic conference once tissue is back.

reports.text: FDG PET-CT. Right upper lobe 4 cm spiculated mass, intensely FDG avid, SUVmax 9.6. No FDG-avid hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes. No abnormal uptake in liver, adrenals or skeleton. Physiologic activity elsewhere.
reports.conclusion: Hypermetabolic RUL mass consistent with primary lung malignancy. No nodal or distant metastatic disease.

documents.title: PET-CT reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: PET copy in: RUL mass avid, no nodes, nothing distant. Biopsy 8/20.

conditions.label: Non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe
conditions.note: adenocarcinoma, clinical stage IB (T2a N0 M0)

procedures.procedure: Percutaneous core needle biopsy of lung

reports.text: Specimen: lung, right upper lobe, CT-guided core biopsy, 3 cores. Microscopic: infiltrating malignant glands with acinar architecture in a desmoplastic stroma. Immunohistochemistry: TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative.

documents.title: Biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Path received: lung adenocarcinoma. With PET, stage IB (T2a N0 M0). Pulmonology has told him; their conference is 9/3. Called him - he's okay, said he'd 'rather know.' Biopsy site fine, no shortness of breath after. Added to problem list.

documents.title: Surveillance cystoscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Outside urology. Office cystoscopy 08/27/2024, received 08/29. History low-grade pTa urothelial carcinoma right lateral wall, TURBT 8/2023; last cystoscopy 11/2023 negative. Flexible cystoscopy: resection scar right lateral wall well healed. No papillary or flat lesions. Urethra normal. Impression: no evidence of recurrence. Next cystoscopy in 1 year. Aware of new lung diagnosis; no change to our plan.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Visit 09/03/2024.
Diagnosis: RUL adenocarcinoma, cT2a N0 M0, stage IB.
Reviewed at multidisciplinary thoracic conference with thoracic surgery and radiation oncology. Given his heart failure and recent weight loss, the group favored stereotactic body radiotherapy over lobectomy. Discussed with patient and daughter today; he prefers SBRT. Referred to radiation oncology, simulation next week. Surveillance CT chest every 3-6 months afterward through radiation oncology.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in to go over everything with me. Understands the cancer is early, hasn't spread, and that radiation was chosen because surgery would be hard on his heart. Simulation done, treatments start 9/23, five sessions. Cough the same, appetite a little better; weight 145 lb, holding.
Mood: worried but sleeping. PHQ-2 1.
Exam: decreased breath sounds R upper field, otherwise clear. No edema.
A/P: RUL adenocarcinoma stage IB - SBRT per rad onc. HFpEF/HTN stable. Encouraged calories, protein shakes fine. Bladder surveillance clear 8/27. Flu, COVID and RSV in October.

documents.title: Radiation oncology treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
Outside radiation oncology. Treatment summary, received 10/08/2024.
Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma right upper lobe, cT2a N0 M0, stage IB.
Treatment: stereotactic body radiotherapy, 50 Gy in 5 fractions, 09/23/2024 to 10/03/2024, 4D-CT planning.
Tolerance: mild fatigue. No esophagitis. No change in breathing.
Follow-up: CT chest at 3 months, then every 6 months for 2 years, then yearly. Allergies NKDA.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu, RSV and COVID given per PCP (RSV indicated with heart failure, age 69). Radiation finished 10/3, says he's just tired. Observed 15 min.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 3 months after SBRT. Comparison 7/24/2024. Treated RUL mass now 2.6 cm with surrounding post-treatment ground-glass change. No new nodules. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Treated RUL lesion decreased in size, now 2.6 cm, with expected post-radiation change. No new disease.

documents.title: Post-SBRT CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rad onc 3-month CT copy: mass shrinking, 2.6 cm, no new disease. Good.

events.reason: blood pressure and heart failure follow-up

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels better than in the summer. Cough much less, eating well, weight back up to 151 lb. Energy returning. No dyspnea beyond baseline, no edema.
Seen 3-month CT - lesion smaller.
Exam: lungs clear, no crackles. Neck veins flat, ankles without swelling.
A/P: Weight loss resolved with treatment. RUL adenocarcinoma s/p SBRT - rad onc surveillance. HTN/HFpEF stable, continue all meds. BMP. Cardiology follow-up next month (annual). RTC spring AWV.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Office visit 01/28/2025. Faxed 04/22/2025 at practice request.

Follow-up for HFpEF and hypertension. 69-year-old with hyperlipidemia and recently treated lung cancer (SBRT fall 2024).
New complaint: aching in both legs, building over two months. Constant and dull, worse with walking, better at rest. No injury.
Meds: metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20. NKDA.
Exam: skin normal over the legs, distal pulses palpable, no edema. Strength 5/5 in all four limbs; tender to palpation over the thigh and hip girdle muscles.
Labs: CK 600 (ref 38-174), AST 40, ALT 45, TSH 2.5, LDL 90.
Assessment: statin-associated muscle symptoms with mild CK elevation. Euvolemic HFpEF.
Plan: hold atorvastatin 4 weeks, repeat CK, then decide on rechallenge.

Addendum 02/25/2025: aches resolved off statin, CK 142. Restarted atorvastatin 40 mg daily as rechallenge; to call if aches return. Annual follow-up.

documents.title: heart doctor stopped my cholesterol pill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The heart doctor said my leg aches might be from the atorvastatin and told me to stop it for a month and get a blood test after. Just so you know. Is that ok with you?

documents.title: RE: heart doctor stopped my cholesterol pill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know. The doctor says that's a reasonable plan - follow cardiology's instructions and keep your other medicines the same. We'll ask their office to send us the visit note.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 6 months after SBRT. Comparison 12/10/2024. Treated RUL lesion now a 2.4 cm consolidative scar-like opacity with linear margins. No new nodules. No adenopathy. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Evolving post-radiation change at the RUL treatment site. No evidence of recurrence or new disease.

documents.title: Surveillance CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 6-month CT reviewed: scar-like change 2.4 cm, nothing new.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Second request to cardiology for the January visit note and labs. They say it was 'not finalized' - will fax when signed.

conditions.label: Statin-associated muscle symptoms
conditions.note: CK 600 on atorvastatin 1/2025; resolved off drug, rechallenged 2/2025 without recurrence

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Cardiology note from January finally arrived last week: CK 600 with leg aches, statin held 4 wks, CK 142 and aches gone, restarted atorva 40 as rechallenge. He says legs fine since restarting. Added statin-associated muscle symptoms to the list.
Function: independent, walking most days. No falls. PHQ-2 0.
Lung ca: 6-month CT stable. Bladder: next scope September.
HTN/HFpEF: BP at goal, weight 152 lb, no edema.
Labs today. Colonoscopy due 2027.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request: lisinopril 20, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, 90-day. Approved with 3 refills.

events.reason: worsening shortness of breath and leg swelling

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Bilateral pleural effusions, layering. Post-treatment scarring right upper lobe, unchanged in character from prior CT. Heart size at upper limits of normal.
Specimen: pleural fluid, right, thoracentesis. Cytology: mesothelial cells, scattered lymphocytes and macrophages.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, a regional hospital. Seen 08/04/2025; faxed to us 08/26/2025.

CC: shortness of breath.
HPI: 70M with heart failure, seen by his cardiologist this year, presenting with a week of progressive breathlessness, about 5 kg weight gain by home scale and worsening swelling of both legs. Lung adenocarcinoma treated with SBRT 2024. Bladder cancer resected 2023.
Meds: lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 22.
Exam: breath sounds reduced at both bases, no crackles. JVP elevated. Pitting edema both legs.
CXR: bilateral pleural effusions.
Given cancer history, diagnostic thoracentesis performed on the right: pleural protein 1.5 g/dL with serum protein 6.0 (ratio <0.5); pleural LDH 110 with serum LDH 200 (ratio <0.6). Transudate by Light's criteria. NT-proBNP 3,420.
Impression: acute decompensated heart failure with bilateral transudative effusions.
Disposition: IV furosemide given, admitted to medicine.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 08/04/2025, discharged 08/07/2025. Received 08/26/2025.
Principal diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure (preserved EF).
Course: diuresed with IV furosemide, net loss 4.5 kg. Breathing back to baseline on room air by day 2. Pleural cytology from the ED thoracentesis negative for malignant cells. Creatinine stable throughout.
Discharge weight 69.5 kg.
Discharge medications: unchanged from home - lisinopril 20 daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 BID, hydrochlorothiazide 25 daily, furosemide 40 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, aspirin 81 daily.
Instructions: weigh daily, call for gain of more than 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week; limit salt. Follow up with PCP within 1 week and cardiology within 1 month.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Daughter calling - admitted
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called: dad was admitted last night through the ER for fluid on the lungs and swelling, his heart failure. They drained fluid from one side. He's feeling better already. Expected home in a couple of days. Will book follow-up within a week of discharge. Asked hospital to fax records.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home since 8/7 after 3 nights in for decompensated heart failure; ED drained fluid from the R chest, he was told it wasn't cancer. Discharge paperwork not here yet - history from pt and daughter and his discharge med sheet. Meds unchanged.
Now: breathing at baseline, sleeping flat, home weight 153 lb daily. Watching salt.
Exam: weight 69.5 kg. Lungs clear. JVP not elevated. Trace ankle edema.
A/P: ADHF, resolved, euvolemic now on home furosemide 40 daily. Daily weights - call for 2 lb/day or 5 lb/week. BMP today. Cardiology follow-up being scheduled by hospital. Will review summary when it arrives.

documents.title: Post-discharge weight check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt one week after his visit. Home weights 152.5-153.5 lb, no swelling, breathing fine, using less salt. Cardiology follow-up booked for September. Reinforced call parameters.

documents.title: Hospital records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED and discharge summary from 8/4-8/7 reviewed. Transudate by Light's criteria, cytology negative, NT-proBNP 3,420. Discharged on home meds. Matches what we did 8/13.

documents.title: Surveillance cystoscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Outside urology. Office cystoscopy 09/09/2025. Low-grade pTa urothelial carcinoma resected 8/2023, prior scopes clear. Bladder mucosa normal throughout; healed scar right lateral wall. No tumor. Next cystoscopy 1 year.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 12 months after SBRT. Comparison 3/11/2025. Right upper lobe post-radiation fibrosis, stable to slightly smaller. No new nodules. No adenopathy. Previously described pleural effusions resolved.

documents.title: 12-month CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: One year out: stable fibrosis, no recurrence, effusions gone.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu and 2025-26 COVID given. Weight log reviewed - steady around 153. No reaction.

events.reason: transient loss of vision right eye

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 21 days

reports.text: Noncontrast head CT. No acute hemorrhage, mass effect or territorial infarct. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. Orbits unremarkable.
Sinus rhythm. Normal intervals. No acute ST changes.

Bilateral carotid duplex. Right internal carotid artery: heterogeneous plaque at the origin with velocities in the 50-69% stenosis range. Left internal carotid artery: no hemodynamically significant stenosis. Vertebral flow antegrade bilaterally.
reports.conclusion: Right ICA stenosis 50-69%. No significant left ICA stenosis.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, a regional hospital. Seen 12/01/2025; faxed 12/03/2025.

CC: vision loss right eye, resolved.
HPI: 70M with heart failure (admitted for decompensation in August), hypertension and hyperlipidemia. About 2 hours before arrival, sudden painless loss of vision in the right eye lasting roughly 10 minutes, then full recovery. No symptoms now. Very shaken by it.
Meds: lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. NKDA.
Exam: visual acuity and fields grossly intact. Fundoscopic exam without abnormality. Neuro exam nonfocal.
CT head: no acute process. ECG: sinus rhythm. Carotid duplex: right ICA 50-69% stenosis, left without significant stenosis.
Impression: amaurosis fugax, right eye, with ipsilateral carotid stenosis.
Plan: continue aspirin, add clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 21 days. Continue statin. Vascular surgery referral. Return for any recurrence, weakness or speech change. Discharged home with daughter.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in ED 12/1 for 10 min of painless vision loss R eye. No repeat episodes. No weakness, numbness or speech trouble. Taking clopidogrel with aspirin, done around 12/22. No bleeding or bruising.
ED record reviewed: CT head neg, ECG sinus, duplex R ICA 50-69%.
Exam: neuro nonfocal. No carotid bruit appreciated. Lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: Amaurosis fugax from R carotid stenosis - resolved. Finish 21 days clopidogrel then aspirin alone. Vascular surgery referral sent today. Atorvastatin 40 continued. BP at goal. Reviewed stroke warning signs with him and daughter - call 911.
